scenario.name: Length-of-Stay Analysis
scenario.description: Complex patients are both more likely to be assigned a specialist and inherently stay longer — a confounding path that makes specialists look worse than they are. CausalOCPM isolates the true causal effect of specialist assignment on length of stay.

executiveSummary.headline: Specialist assignment is the dominant causal driver of length of stay — statistically validated, not just correlated.
bullets: Recovered causal effect 5.25 days via Double ML vs a planted ground truth of 5.27 — recovery error 0.4%. A naive dashboard would have reported 6.01; confounding accounts for 0.76 of that.
Autonomous bootstrapped-PC discovery: F1 0.83 (7 of 9 planted edges, 1 spurious). Domain knowledge then recovers the 2 missed edges and re-orients the spurious one — never inventing a relationship.
Recommended action: Guarantee specialist consult within 12 hours of request → ~$610K/yr expected savings, payback 2.3 months
Robust to hidden confounding: VanderWeele E-value ≈ 7.1, placebo test +0.02 ≈ 0, stable across 10 regenerated datasets

cate.note: The binary specialist-assignment effect within each patient-complexity tertile (mediators fixed); small by construction — the 5.25-day figure is the full path effect through Treatment Duration. The effect rises with complexity, so an SLA targeted at the most complex admissions returns most.

sensitivity.verdict: The effect stays positive across an assumed-confounding sweep out to 30% strength (5.25 → 1.11 days). Placebo +0.02 ≈ 0; random common cause re-estimates 5.25. VanderWeele E-value ≈ 7.1.
